find.description: Find tasks in the workspace-local store by text, semantic state and labels, in creation order, one bounded page at a time.

get.description: Read one task of the workspace-local store.

create.description: Record a task in the workspace-local store. A repeated idempotency key returns the task it created; the same key with other content is a conflict.

update.description: Change a local task's title, body or labels. expectedRevision is compared and written under the store's exclusive lock; a change that alters nothing keeps the revision.

transition.description: Move a local task to another state. expectedRevision is compared and written under the store's exclusive lock. Assignment, hierarchy and exclusive claims are not offered by this provider.

find.description: Find the local proposals recorded for an exact repository, base and head. The repository defaults to the binding's repository setting, else "local".

upsert.description: Record or update the one open local proposal for an exact repository, base and head in the workspace-local store. Nothing is pushed or opened on a hosting service, and merge is not offered.

status.description: Read a local proposal and the reviews recorded for it. The local provider runs no hosted checks: checks are always reported unsupported.

review.description: Record a review of a local proposal. A repeated idempotency key returns the review it recorded; nothing is published to a hosting service.

sync.description: Publish an agent session's state and plan to its local mission, then read the mission and the inbox. Before it answers, the store takes the decision answers and messages its owner wrote as files in the store directory; nothing leaves the machine.

ask.description: Ask the local mission's owner one decision. The owner answers it by writing answers/<decision>.json in the store directory. A repeated idempotency key returns the decision already recorded; the same key with other content is a conflict.

reply.description: Reply to one message of the local mission's inbox. A message takes one reply: the same reply again changes nothing, and another reply is a conflict.

status.description: Read a local mission's view and a page of its sessions, with each session's state, stage, usage, branch, and error or waitUntil, newest first. It reads the store as the last write left it and takes no owner file.

context.description: Load the memory records relevant to an identity, kinds and the resolved project selection: each record's identity, kind and scope decide, never where the backend keeps it. One bounded page in kind-then-id order; freshness says when each record changed and when it was read. The binding's settings choose the backend: a store directory (file) or a branch of a Git repository (git). Only the git backend with a remote reaches the network.

mission.description: Read one mission's checkpointed record with its revision, provenance and freshness. The binding's settings choose the backend: a store directory (file) or a branch of a Git repository (git). Only the git backend with a remote reaches the network.

checkpoint.description: Save a mission checkpoint against its expected revision, or create the mission with mustNotExist. The comparison and the write are one step (under the store lock for file, a conditional ref update or a leased push for git), so of two writers at one revision exactly one lands and the other gets a conflict. A repeated idempotency key replays the write it produced. A push whose outcome is unknown is reconciled by reading the branch again; when that fails the checkpoint is unresolved. Evidence entries are references: this provider never records that anything passed. The binding's settings choose the backend: a store directory (file) or a branch of a Git repository (git). Only the git backend with a remote reaches the network.

search.description: Find memory records whose title or content contains the query, ignoring case, under the same selection as context. One bounded page in kind-then-id order; no index is kept. The binding's settings choose the backend: a store directory (file) or a branch of a Git repository (git). Only the git backend with a remote reaches the network.
